claims.text: Lattice distortion induced by atomic-size misfit is the primary factor governing hardness and strength in high-entropy alloys.
Atomic-size misfit among constituent elements induces lattice distortion.
Impeded dislocation motion strengthens the alloy.
Constituent elements with relatively similar atomic sizes produce minimal lattice distortion.
Incrementally increasing atomic-size differences through composition changes will increase lattice distortion.
Identical casting and annealing conditions will help ensure a uniform and comparable microstructure across the alloys.
Increasing atomic-size misfit produces higher lattice strain.
Higher lattice strain raises the barrier to dislocation movement.
The resulting resistance to dislocation movement enhances hardness through solid-solution strengthening.
The resulting resistance to dislocation movement enhances tensile yield strength through solid-solution strengthening.
Alloys with greater atomic-size misfit will have higher Vickers hardness than a minimal-misfit baseline when phase structure and microstructure are preserved.
Alloys with greater atomic-size misfit will have higher tensile yield strength than a minimal-misfit baseline when phase structure and microstructure are preserved.
The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase high-entropy alloys without significant secondary phases or precipitates.
The proposed relationship may not apply at high temperatures or under extreme alloying conditions that cause phase transformations or local ordering.
Local chemical ordering, minor precipitation, and dislocation-density changes may influence the magnitude of strengthening associated with lattice distortion.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires systematic modification of alloy composition, while the falsification design says substituted alloys should retain an identical overall composition. Elemental substitution necessarily changes elemental composition unless 'overall composition' only means a separately defined quantity such as total atomic fraction; that meaning is not specified.
